intro: Sunday June 21. US markets reopen Monday June 22 — the most consequential session of the post-FOMC recovery. The week's catalyst density is extraordinary: June 22 is the DXY gate decision + IBIT flow confirmation + SPCX IG pricing event; June 24 is a dual-catalyst day (Micron Q3 earnings and NVDA Annual Meeting simultaneously, a coincidence not seen since February 2026); June 25 is PCE. The macro setup has improved each day of the 3-day closure: SPX futures at 7,556.25 (+0.74%), BTC tracking a fourth consecutive UTC day above $63,500 (session low $63,895.93 — never tested stop), SK Hynix ADR SEC clearance expected any day this week. The ideas below are calibrated for the June 22 open. Three scenarios diverge: (A) DXY closes below 100 on June 22 + IBIT shows net inflow → execute NVDA conditional add, upgrade BTC to medium-high, SPCX opens above $185; (B) DXY holds above 100, BTC consolidates → hold defensive posture and arrive positioned for June 24 dual catalyst; (C) 30Y breaks above 5.00% or Micron pre-announces miss → step-aside across high-multiple names. The June 24 dual catalyst (Micron Q3 + NVDA Annual Meeting) is the week's override event — position before June 24, not after.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: ADR SEC clearance imminent (week of June 22) — any official confirmation triggers institutional pre-positioning before the August Nasdaq listing; add on any June 23 KOSPI pullback to ₩2,688,000–₩2,750,000.
ideas.why: SK Hynix ADR SEC regulatory clearance is now expected the week of June 22 — the announcement could come any day this week before or during the June 23 KOSPI open. The actual Nasdaq listing is targeting August 2026 with a potential $14 billion raise. A $14B US-listed ADR creates a structural new demand channel: US passive index funds and institutional mandates that cannot hold KRX-listed shares gain direct access, with index rebalancing demand potentially representing ₩100T+ in forced buying. Additionally, Micron Q3 earnings on June 24 (EPS $19.72 est., revenue $34.52B) will be processed by buy-side before the June 25 KOSPI open — a MU beat-and-raise on HBM demand (SK Hynix holds 58% global HBM share) would catalyze a June 25 gap-up. All 38 analysts still below current price (₩2,764,000 vs ₩2,690,000 consensus) — the PT revision cascade is mandatory and accelerating with each new ADR development.
ideas.trigger: June 23 KOSPI open: any pullback to ₩2,688,000–₩2,750,000 (June 19 session floor zone) → add immediately; stop ₩2,540,000. Also: if SK Hynix issues an official ADR SEC clearance filing or announcement before June 23 KOSPI open → add at any price on the June 23 open (ADR clearance removes execution uncertainty from the thesis). If Goldman or BofA issues a ₩3.0M+ PT note before June 23 KOSPI open → add at any price on open.
ideas.risk: ADR SEC clearance delayed beyond week of June 22 (positions built around imminent clearance unwind on delay headline); Micron Q3 miss on HBM demand before June 25 KOSPI open (direct read-through negative); Samsung announces a specific NVIDIA HBM4E qualification win before SK Hynix completes qualification.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: June 22 conditional-add decision day (DXY 23 bps from gate) + June 24 dual override catalyst (Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 on same day) — the post-FOMC recovery's most important week.
ideas.why: DXY declined to ~100.23 on weekend FX (from 100.79 Thursday) — the conditional-add gate is 23 bps away. SPX futures at 7,556.25 (+0.74%) suggest a risk-on June 22 open that keeps VIX and SPX gates cleared. If DXY confirms below 100.00 on June 22 close, ALL THREE gates clear simultaneously and the $205–$215 add executes at the confirmed close. NVDA's last official close of $210.69 is already within the add zone. The June 24 dual catalyst is structurally significant: Micron Q3 earnings (EPS $19.72 est., revenue $34.52B) and the NVDA Annual Meeting (Jensen Huang, 9 AM PT) on the same day creates a 'demand signal + management conviction' compound event. Jensen's first post-FOMC public commentary on AI capex durability can trigger a $10–$20 single-day move independent of the DXY gate status.
ideas.trigger: June 22 session close: DXY below 100.00 AND VIX below 17 on the same session → execute add at $205–$215, stop $195. Override trigger: Annual Meeting June 24, Jensen explicitly bullish on AI capex in hawkish rate environment → add regardless of gate status. Pre-position before June 24 (arrive before the session, not at open).
ideas.risk: DXY reverses the weekend decline on June 22 open (Warsh hawkish Fed speech, strong PMI data); Micron Q3 misses on HBM demand ($34.52B bar is elevated after 3.1% revision) or warns on Q4; 30Y breaks above 5.00% before June 22 close.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Fourth consecutive UTC day above $63,500 stop (June 21 session low $63,895 — never tested stop); IBIT June 22 flow data is the size-upgrade trigger; demand zone has shifted structurally higher.
ideas.why: BTC is live at $64,460.58 (11:02 UTC June 21, Crypto.com MCP), tracking a fourth consecutive UTC day above the $63,500 stop. The June 21 UTC session low of $63,895.93 is $395.93 above the stop — vs June 20's low of $63,178.28 which briefly breached the stop by $321.72. The demand zone has shifted structurally upward from $63,000–$63,500 to $63,500–$64,000, signaling organic institutional accumulation. The stop framework has progressed through four phases: trigger → survival → stabilization → confirmation. The June 22 US session is the critical follow-through: IBIT ETF flow data (first post-Juneteenth print) is the institutional confirmation event; a second consecutive net inflow day confirms the $86M June 12 inflow was the start of a sustained reversal. SPX futures +0.74% and DXY at 100.23 (approaching <100 gate) support the risk-on environment for June 22.
ideas.trigger: June 22 US session open: check IBIT flow on farside.co.uk — second consecutive net inflow day = add 25% at market (size-up at $63,500–$65,000 range); DXY confirm below 100.00 on June 22 close = macro gate clears; BTC close above $65,000 on June 22 = double-bottom confirmed, target $67,000. Active stop: $63,500 UTC daily close.
ideas.risk: June 22 IBIT flow shows resumed outflows (false reversal); BTC closes below $63,500 on June 21 UTC midnight in the remaining hours (afternoon UTC session risk); DXY reverses above 101 on June 22 open; Fear & Greed Index stays below 20 (Extreme Fear) even as price improves, signaling retail distribution into institutional bids.

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: Q3 earnings June 24 (same day as NVDA Annual Meeting) — EPS consensus $19.72, revenue $34.52B (31 analysts); beat-and-raise on HBM demand is the week's primary semiconductor read-through.
ideas.why: Micron reports Q3 fiscal year 2026 earnings on June 24 — the same day as the NVDA Annual Meeting, creating a dual AI semiconductor catalyst. Street expects EPS $19.72 and revenue $34.52B (consensus revised up 3.1% in past 30 days). MU holds 21% global HBM market share and is the most direct US-listed proxy for AI memory demand. If MU beats revenue and raises guidance with strong HBM commentary (demand accelerating, ASPs holding), it simultaneously validates NVDA's Blackwell/Vera Rubin supply chain and SK Hynix's HBM4E market position. The post-FOMC selloff gave MU a better entry than pre-FOMC — AI memory demand is not rate-sensitive, and the FOMC selloff represents mispriced fundamentals, not a change in AI capex.
ideas.trigger: Pre-earnings: buy MU at $95–$105 before June 24 with stop at $90 daily close; position for beat-and-raise. Post-earnings on June 24: if MU beats and guides above consensus → hold for post-earnings momentum leg; if MU misses or guides down on HBM → exit immediately and reassess NVDA/SK Hynix long theses.
ideas.risk: MU misses the elevated $34.52B bar (revised up 3.1%) on HBM ASPs or Q4 volume guidance; FOMC rate path uncertainty causing enterprise IT budget pressure that reduces cloud customer HBM demand; Samsung HBM market share gaining faster than MU's consensus model implies.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Step aside; June 22 is the diagnostic for 72+ hours of unpriced IG ratings — monitor for two consecutive closes above $185; SPX futures +0.74% supports a gap-up open.
ideas.why: SpaceX investment-grade ratings (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+) have been unpriced for 72+ hours due to Juneteenth + Saturday + Sunday market closure. June 22 is the first and only opportunity for equity markets to price these ratings simultaneously with an SPX futures backdrop of +0.74%. The Moody's Baa1 (above Tesla's Baa3) is the week's most underappreciated catalyst for SPCX — it validates the franchise quality above the most recognized IG industrial-tech precedent. The $185 daily close stop triggered at $174.90 on June 18, but the IG ratings + improving macro create conditions for a gap toward or above $185 on June 22 open. DXY at ~100.23 reduces the rate-discount compression on the 84x multiple. If SPCX opens at or above $185 and produces two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume — that re-entry sequence begins.
ideas.trigger: June 22 open: if SPCX opens $175–$185 with >150M shares → begin stabilization watch (do not buy yet); if SPCX produces first close above $185 → monitor for second close (required); two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume = re-entry with stop $165 and July put hedge. SPCX opens below $165 → correction extending, wait for $150–$160.
ideas.risk: DXY reverses above 101 on June 22 open (removes the dual cost-of-capital positive narrative); MSCI passive bid fully exhausted (Day 11+) leaving retail as marginal buyer; SPX broad market selloff on June 22 reverses the futures improvement; Jim Chanos valuation thesis — 84x revenue with net losses — still valid even after IG ratings.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: Best post-FOMC dip buy in megacap — SPX futures +0.74% + DXY declining + IBIT outflows ended = ideal macro backdrop for the highest-beta, self-funded AI megacap.
ideas.why: Meta fell -5.44% on June 17 FOMC day — the largest FOMC-session loss in the Magnificent-7. SPX futures at +0.74% for June 22 open represent the clearest macro buy signal since the selloff. Meta's fundamentals remain the cleanest in big tech: AI capex funded entirely from operations, no external debt, strong ad revenue acceleration, and the cheapest forward multiple in the Mag-7 post-selloff. The convergence of IBIT outflows ending (improving institutional risk appetite), DXY declining (positive for international advertising revenue), and SPX futures pointing to a risk-on June 22 open precisely mirrors the conditions that preceded the last three post-FOMC megacap recoveries. META's self-funded AI model makes it the least rate-sensitive Mag-7 name and the first destination for institutional capital returning to megacap.
ideas.trigger: June 22 open: VIX stays below 17 (on track at 16.41 weekend) AND DXY shows further decline from 100.23 → buy META at $545–$560, stop $530 daily close. If DXY reverses above 101 on June 22 open: stand aside on META. June 24 dual catalyst (Micron + NVDA Annual Meeting) is the secondary catalyst that can extend META's recovery if AI capex narrative is confirmed.
ideas.risk: 30Y Treasury tests 5.00% before or during June 22-26 → multiple compression across all long-duration growth assets; June 22 post-FOMC Week 2 historical pattern (8-of-9 weakest) reverses the futures improvement; AI regulatory headlines (antitrust, EU data privacy) creating specific META headwind.

ideas.name: SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF
ideas.idea: Iran ceasefire in effect; Brent at $80.59 structurally below H2 energy equity model assumptions; H2 estimate cuts not yet in sell-side consensus; DXY declining is a commodity-equity headwind.
ideas.why: The Iran ceasefire formal signing confirmed the Hormuz reopening timeline (30 days for mine-clearance). Brent at $80.59 (latest print) is structurally below the $87–$90 embedded in H2 2026 energy equity models — sell-side analysts have not yet revised H2 estimates down by the required 8–12%. Even with Brent $1.59 higher than prior $79 estimate, the structural gap between current Brent and H2 model Brent remains $6–9. SPX futures +0.74% suggests a risk-on June 22 open — which is typically associated with DXY declining, a slight headwind for oil in dollar terms. The Warsh hawkish FOMC compounds the XLE short: risk-off commodity demand uncertainty + oil supply increase from Hormuz reopening is a triple headwind for energy equities.
ideas.trigger: June 22: if XLE opens at $53–$56 with Brent below $83 → initiate or add to short; any Brent bounce to $82–$84 on Hormuz mine-clearance delay headlines is the premium short entry. Cover only if Brent closes above $90 on two consecutive sessions (Hormuz supply addition fails).
ideas.risk: Iran ceasefire collapses; Hormuz mine-clearance delayed beyond 60 days; OPEC+ announces unexpected additional production cuts; Brent spikes above $90 on a non-Hormuz supply shock (Libya, Nigeria disruption).

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Post-FOMC dip at $375–$390 — Azure AI monetization compounds regardless of rate path; least rate-sensitive megacap AI play in the Mag-7.
ideas.why: Microsoft fell ~3.79% on June 17 FOMC day. At ~$378, Azure AI monetization and Copilot attach rates compound on a subscription-revenue model that is largely rate-insensitive (contracted enterprise bookings at set prices for 12-36 months). SPX futures +0.74% + IBIT outflows ending + DXY declining = improving risk appetite for the recovery trade. MSFT is the safest vehicle for investors who want exposure without the tail risk of NVDA (gate-dependent add) or BTC (stop-framework). The recurring-revenue enterprise model provides the clearest P/E support in the Mag-7 at current levels. Azure AI acceleration commentary from June 24 megacap sector sentiment (Micron + NVDA Annual Meeting) is the secondary catalyst.
ideas.trigger: VIX stays below 17 on June 22 AND MSFT holds $375 support → buy at $375–$390, stop $368 daily close. If June 24 Micron + NVDA catalysts confirm AI capex durability → raise MSFT conviction to medium and extend hold.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends beyond H2 2026; antitrust scrutiny of OpenAI relationship limits bundling; 30Y above 5.00% compresses all long-duration growth multiples in the megacap cohort.
